title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a programmatic sketch, numbered 1°–4°. It appears to aim at describing a Dieudonné-type crystal in characteristic p by 'linear algebra' data on the Zariski site, twisted by Frobenius. My reading of the notation is uncertain throughout.

Header scribbles:
- An inclusion of crystalline sites X_cris,0 ↪ X_cris/n, presumably crystals relative to F_p versus Z/p^n.
- A short exact sequence 0 → G → G' → G'' → 0, plausibly finite flat groups embedded in BT groups, or a resolution.
- A map M'' → M'.
These suggest the setting of Grothendieck's 1970 programme on Barsotti–Tate groups and Dieudonné crystals: the Montreal lectures and the ICM Nice talk.

1°) A crystal M of finite presentation on S_cris/F_p, with F_M and V_M.
- From these it produces two triangles. I(M) is L'(M) → L.(M) → Δ*(M)^(p). II(M) is L.(M) → L'(M) → Δ*(M), with the roles rotated.
- Write ε*(M) = M for the value on S (Zariski realisation); φ is the absolute Frobenius of S.
- The natural reading: Δ*(M)^(p) and Δ*(M) are Frobenius-twisted realisations of M linked by F and V. The L-objects play the role of Lie/co-Lie pieces, i.e. kernels and images of F and V.
- Classically, for a BT_1 with Dieudonné module D: Ker F = Im V ≅ ω (Hodge filtration) and Im F = Ker V (conjugate filtration). The Frobenius-semilinear identifications of the graded pieces are exactly an F-zip structure.
- Writing these as two distinguished triangles, rather than two filtrations, is a derived formulation.

2°) The target notion: 'triangles' T: T_0 → T_1 → T. on S_Zar of perfect complexes of amplitude in [-1,0], possibly with extra F–V structure ('F-V-triangles?').
- Amplitude [-1,0] perfect complexes are what Illusie's co-Lie complex of a finite locally free group scheme is.
- So T is presumably meant to be built from Lie complexes, e.g. of G, G', G''.

3°) An isomorphism α: φ*(T) ≅ I(M).

4°) An isomorphism β: T_1 ≅ ε*(Δ*(M)), with a compatibility. The component α_1: φ*(T_1) → Δ*(M)^(p) must equal φ*(β) followed by the canonical φ*ε*Δ*(M) ≅ Δ*(M)^(p).

The problem served is probably one of two:
- reconstructing (or classifying) the Dieudonné crystal mod p — equivalently the BT_1 or finite group — from Zariski data (a Frobenius-twisted triangle plus descent-type identification); or
- comparing the crystalline invariant with the Lie-complex invariant.

It stops at the definition stage; no theorem or proof appears.
errors: No mathematical errors can be pinpointed: it is a list of definitions and desiderata with question marks ('ou F-V-triangles?', 'ou F-V-isom?').
The exact meaning of Δ*, L., L' cannot be fixed from this page alone.
The roles of I(M) and II(M) (rotated triangles) are not reconciled with the single data T. Only I(M) is matched in 3°; II(M) is left unused, which is a gap in the sketch.

ideas.what: Dieudonné crystals of finite presentation over S_cris/F_p with F and V; relation to finite flat / BT groups (the 0→G→G'→G''→0 header)
ideas.where_published: Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Montréal 1970/74); ICM Nice 1970 talk

ideas.what: Encoding F and V of a mod-p crystal as two triangles linking a Frobenius twist Δ*(M)^(p), Δ*(M) and Lie-type pieces
ideas.modern_name: F-zip (two filtrations with Frobenius-linear identification of graded pieces), written in derived/triangle form
ideas.usually_credited_to: Moonen–Wedhorn (2004) for F-zips; Kraft, Oort for the BT_1 linear algebra

ideas.what: Triangles of perfect complexes of amplitude [-1,0] on S_Zar with Frobenius-twisted isomorphisms to crystal-derived triangles, as descent-type data
ideas.modern_name: Derived F-zips / co-Lie complex description of finite flat group schemes; precursor of display/window-type and F-gauge descriptions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie (co-Lie complex, 1972); Zink (displays, 2002); Yaylali (derived F-zips, ~2022); Drinfeld, Bhatt–Lurie (F-gauges)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches classifying a mod-p Dieudonné crystal by Frobenius-twisted triangles of perfect complexes of amplitude [-1,0] on the Zariski site. This is essentially a derived version of F-zips, about 35 years before F-zips and 50 before derived F-zips. The programme (steps 1°–4°) is left unfinished on this page.
missed.quote: Triangles ... sur S_Zar de complexes parfaits d'ampl. [-1,0] ... φ*(T) ≃^α I(M) ... T_1 ≃^β ε*(Δ*(M))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck considering a derived, Zariski-local 'F-zip'-type invariant of crystals and Lie complexes. This is historically relevant to derived F-zips and F-gauges, and to linking Illusie's co-Lie complex with Dieudonné theory, a link made only partially in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: Conjectural reading, but the structure — two F/V triangles involving a Frobenius twist, perfect complexes of amplitude [-1,0], and compatibility of φ* with restriction — anticipates F-zip / derived F-zip ideas not attributed to Grothendieck. It is only a definitional sketch with question marks, so the surprise is moderate.
transcription_corrections: The exact sequence in the header likely begins with '0 →': '0 → G ↪ G' ↠ G'' → 0'.
The header map 'M'' → M^•' is maybe 'M'' → M'' (unclear in the image).
'd'où [?]' is probably just 'd'où'; the crossed-out symbol before 'avec' looks like a struck 'Δ' or 'B'.
'd'ampl. parfaite [?] C[-1,0]' should probably read 'd'ampl. parfaite ⊂ [-1,0]' (amplitude contained in [-1,0]).
'et qui soit commutatif' is probably 'et qu'il soit commutatif le diagramme', followed by the diagram whose vertical arrow is labelled 'id'.
In 4°, the arrow α_1: φ*(T_1) → Δ*(M)^(p) is written with an underlined/blackened Δ, possibly distinguishing a variant Δ*.
